name: Moebius Syndrome-Axonal Neuropathy-Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism Syndrome
aliases: Moebius Syndrome with Axonal Neuropathy and Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Moebius Syndrome-Axonal Neuropathy-Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Congenital bilateral facial nerve (cranial nerve VII) palsy causing facial paralysis
Electrophysiological evidence of axonal sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy
Clinical and biochemical evidence of hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with low gonadotropins and sex steroids
Restricted horizontal eye movements due to abducens nerve (cranial nerve VI) involvement
Mild to moderate developmental delay or intellectual disability

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital bilateral facial nerve palsy, axonal neuropathy confirmed by electrophysiology, and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by electrophysiological and hormonal studies; genetic testing may assist but no definitive gene identified

laboratory: Low serum luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH)
Low serum testosterone or estradiol depending on sex
Normal routine blood counts and metabolic panels
imaging: MRI brain may show hypoplasia of cranial nerve nuclei
Nerve conduction studies showing reduced amplitude consistent with axonal neuropathy
genetic: No consistent pathogenic variants identified; possible sporadic or multifactorial etiology

distinguishingFeatures: Primarily congenital facial and abducens nerve palsy
Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with anosmia or hyposmia
No facial nerve palsy or axonal neuropathy
Normal cranial nerve function except olfactory

redFlags: Progressive respiratory insufficiency due to bulbar dysfunction
Severe feeding difficulties leading to failure to thrive
Early onset hypogonadism with absent puberty
references: Orphanet: Moebius syndrome-axonal neuropathy-hypogonadotropic hypogonadism syndrome, ORPHA:2560
Verzijl HT, et al. Moebius syndrome with axonal neuropathy and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism: a distinct clinical entity. Neurology. 2005.
National Organization for Rare Disorders (NORD) - Moebius Syndrome
